headline: Record revenue on restarts, earnings dip on mark-to-market
summary_short: Alcoa's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 24.2% q/q to a record $3,966M on restart-driven aluminum shipments and higher realized prices, but GAAP net income fell 4.2% q/q to $407M ($1.53 diluted EPS) on mark-to-market losses on Ma'aden shares and energy contracts.
summary_long: Revenue hit a record $3,966M (+24.2% q/q): Aluminum revenue +31% on restart-driven shipments (San Ciprián, Alumar, Lista, Portland) and higher realized prices; Alumina revenue -3% on lower bauxite offtake volumes/pricing. Adjusted EBITDA ex-special-items rose 51% q/q to $901M on higher aluminum prices, partly offset by Pinjarra refinery cost pressure, import tariffs, and energy costs. GAAP net income fell 4.2% q/q to $407M ($1.53/sh) on mark-to-market losses on Ma'aden shares and energy derivatives; adjusted EPS was $2.12. Cash held flat at $1,352M after redeeming $219M of 2028 notes; free cash flow was $422M. Alcoa cut FY2026 alumina production/shipment guidance on Pinjarra/Cyclone Narelle disruption; aluminum segment guidance held.

drivers.explanation: Aluminum segment revenue +31% q/q on higher shipments (incl. value-add product) and higher realized third-party prices; Alumina revenue -3% q/q on lower bauxite offtake volumes and pricing, partly offset by favorable currency.

GAAP EBITDA was roughly flat q/q; the release's separately-defined Adjusted EBITDA (ex-special-items) rose 51% q/q on higher aluminum prices. The gap is $155M of Q2 special items excluded from the adjusted figure.

Unfavorable mark-to-market changes on Ma'aden shares and energy contracts, unfavorable currency impacts, unfavorable energy impacts, and higher Alumina production costs, partially offset by higher aluminum prices and shipments.
Mirrors the net income decline: Ma'aden and energy-contract mark-to-market losses plus unfavorable currency and Alumina cost impacts, partly offset by higher aluminum prices and shipments.

Operating cash flow of $608M was offset by financing outflows (2028 notes redemption $219M, short-term debt repayment $109M, dividends $26M) and investing outflows (capex $186M, equity contributions $40M).
Management cited strong financial results from favorable aluminum prices plus progress on strategic initiatives, most notably the announced South32 (AliGroup) acquisition agreement.
